title: Smart Brevity: The Power of Saying More with Less
author: Jim VandeHei
Mike Allen
Roy Schwartz
target_audience: Anyone seeking to communicate clearly and efficiently
primary_purpose: To guide readers on how to strip away unnecessary words and communicate in a clear, concise, and impactful manner to gain and keep attention in a fast-paced, information-saturated world.

structure_format.organization: Organized into thematic chapters, each addressing an aspect of effective brief communication

key_concepts_lessons: Attention is the new currency in the digital age; winning it requires fast, clear communication.
Most people say too much — editing your message down enhances impact.
Structure your writing for scanning (headers, bolding, lists) to facilitate comprehension.
Lead with the most important takeaway (the ‘nut graf’), not with background or buildup.
Brevity does not mean oversimplification — it means eliminating wasted words while preserving meaning.
Effective brevity is a learned skill that benefits teams, organizations, and personal productivity.
notable_features: Signature ‘Smart Brevity’ format, used by the authors’ media company (Axios)
Visual formatting cues (bold, bullet points) as instructional tools
Actionable frameworks applicable to email, presentations, meetings, and content creation
Addresses both individual and organizational communication strategies
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 2020s, amidst the explosion of digital content and communication channels, the book reflects a growing demand for information efficiency and attention management in business and everyday life. The authors’ experience in political and digital journalism (Politico, Axios) shapes the approach.
reception_impact: Widely praised for actionable, no-nonsense advice relevant to modern professionals
Adopted by organizations aiming to streamline internal and external communications
Appreciated for its readable format and immediately applicable techniques
Some critique that the principles may not fit all professional domains or creative writing
comparable_titles: Made to Stick by Chip Heath & Dan Heath
On Writing Well by William Zinsser
Writing That Works by Kenneth Roman & Joel Raphaelson
